links.reason: The verbal echo is real: நில்லா உலகத்து நிலைமை தூக்கி in the idyll and நில்லாது செல்வம் in the quatrain, with பெற்றவை பிறர்பிறர்க்கு ஆர்த்தி matching பல்லாரோடு உண்க. But the claim that impermanence moves the king to keep the guest rests on giving பல புலந்து and நிலைமை தூக்கி to the king, which the marker himself calls uncertain syntax, so the 'both ends of the gift' point needs a generous reading.

The triad is really shared: Puram 55 ஞாயிற்றன்ன, திங்கள் அன்ன, வானத்தன்ன against Kali 100 சுடரே போல் கொடுமை, மதி என்னத் தண்மை, சுரந்த வான் பொழிந்தற்றா, and கோல் கோடாது answers முறை செய்தி. But the note misdescribes Kali 100: the three praises undone by tears, bangles and pallor are truthfulness (பொய் கூறாய்), giving (the rain) and justice (முறை), not sun, moon and rain, so 'each term hostage' is only partly true.

The figure is distinctive and nearly verbatim: நெடியோன் கொப்பூழ் நான்முக ஒருவற் பயந்த பல்லிதழ்த் தாமரைப் பொகுட்டின் for Kanchi and மாயோன் கொப்பூழ் மலர்ந்த தாமரை ... அரும் பொகுட்கு அனைத்தே அண்ணல் கோயில் for Madurai. That it serves two capitals shows a convention of city praise. The idyll makes the tall-mansioned town (நெடுநகர்) the pericarp, while the fragment maps streets and palace part by part, a difference the teaches sentence smooths over without falsifying.

Both make retribution quick and come of itself: Kural 319 பிற்பகல் தாமே வரும, and the quatrain இம்மையால் செய்ததை இம்மையே ஆம். The pairing shows the impersonal rule voiced as a wronged wife's satisfaction at rivals who நலிந்த her (சுடப்பட்ட வாறு), a real change of use. The sense of சுடப்பட்ட is uncertain, but the retribution claim in lines 1-2 does not depend on it.

The balance word is shared: ஞெமன்கோல் அன்ன செம்மைத்து of the அறங்கூறு அவையம் against தெரிகோல் ஞமன்ன் போல ஒரு திறம் பற்றல் இலியரோ wished on the king. The idyll moves the impartiality to a court and names what it must put away (அச்சமும் அவலமும் ஆர்வமும் ... செற்றமும் உவகையும்), which Puram 6 does not, so the teaches sentence is true and specific.
links.text_issue: purananuru:6 line 9 ஞமன்ன் has a doubled final consonant, probably a misprint for ஞமன்.

links.reason: The only bond is the stock hyperbole of measure: நின் புகழ் கொள்ளாது இம் மலர் தலை உலகே and இடமெல்லாம் கொள்ளாத் தகைத்தே. Neither verse limits the other, and the claim that the Kural takes a praise formula of abundance and fixes it on destitution is a construction about borrowing that the two lines cannot support.

There is a real verbal contrast: Naladiyar 85 has deeds of உம்மை punished இம்மை, while the quatrain says those who hold உம்மையே ஆம் do not understand (ஓரார்காண்). But the quatrain hedges with போலும் and is a wife's taunt about her rivals, not a doctrine, and the two claims can both be held, so 'a live disagreement in the didactic age' overstates it.

Two adjacent poems of one decade to the bard: 131 makes the bond good only கௌவை எழாஅக் காலே, and 132 says the town is now அலர் ஆகின்று over அவர் அருளும் ஆறே. The step from condition to breach is in the Tamil, and the point that the gossip feeds on his grace, not his neglect, rests on அருளும் ஆறே.

The wording is near identical: மாக்கடல் நீக்கிக் கடம்பு அறுத்து இயற்றிய வலம்படு வியன்பணை against மால்கடல் ஓட்டிக் கடம்பு அறுத்து இயற்றிய பண்ணமை முரசின். The note says exactly what the akam poet does with the puram fact: the drum's roar (கண் அதிர்ந்தன்ன) measures the street's கவ்வை. This is the real kind of puram-name link.

The echo is close: நில்லாமையே நிலையிற்று against நில்லாதவற்றை நிலையின என்றுணரும். The teaches sentence is true and good: the friend turns the truth of impermanence to consolation, since the pallor (பசப்பு) cannot stay. But this applies the idea in a new domain and adds no condition to the Kural, so the type should be develops.

Kuru 37 has one tusker stripping யா for his hungry mate (பிடிபசி களைஇய), and Kali 11 has the tusker that lets the பிடி drink first (பிடி ஊட்டிப் பின் உண்ணும் களிறு), then adds the dove and the stag, all reported as his own words (உரைத்தனரே) and argued from by the heroine. The move from the friend's single proof to a catalogue in the heroine's mouth is in the text. Both poems are ascribed to a பெருங்கடுங்கோ/பெருங்கொடுங்கோன், which the note could have used.

The phrase is shared (ஊரறி கௌவை and ஊரறிந்த கெளவை), and its sign is opposite: a threat in the friend's warning (இரவரின் ... கௌவை தரும்), welcomed by the man in the Kural. But these are different speakers' attitudes in different moves of the plot, which the brief says is not a tension. The friend's warning and the man's welcome can both push toward marriage.

Kural 90 makes the host's look decide the guest (முகந்திரிந்து நோக்கக் குழையும் விருந்து). The idyll gives the reverse from a whole town: கண்டோர் எல்லாம் அமர்ந்து இனிது நோக்கி, விருந்து இறை அவரவர் எதிர்கொள, before any gift. The extension from one household's face to the town's look as a mark of the patron's realm is specific and true to the lines.

The conflict is real and explicit. The Vedic logician lists ten அளவை and has perception grasp நாமம் சாதி குணம் கிரியை (27.23-24). Aravanar keeps two means (அளவை இரண்டே), defines perception as சுட்டுணர்வு and says விட்டனர் நாம சாதி குணம் கிரியைகள், which reach அனுமானம் (29.47-51). The teaches sentence names the disputed point accurately.

Both have the owl's cry as a night fear: கூகை ... அஞ்சு வரக் கடுங் குரல் and குன்றக் கூகை குழறினும் அஞ்சும். But the owl is a common night-fear figure, and the role split in the teaches sentence is inexact: in Natrinai 83 the friend speaks for both who wait awake (எம் காதலர் வரல் நசைஇத் துஞ்சாது), so it is not the friend alone who still fears while the girl has passed beyond fear.

Both Vaiyai songs stage the priests refusing the festival flood. In song 6, புலம் புரி அந்தணர் கலங்கினர் over flowers, roots, the food of பூரிய மாக்கள் and நறவம். In the fragment, பார்ப்பார், அந்தணர் and ஐயர் each name one stain, toddy, wedding scent and honey. That every stain is a sign of the town's feast is true of both lists, so the set-piece claim is well supported.

The opposition is real and specific: in Kuru 137 the curse for leaving is இரவலர் வாரா வைகல், and in Akam 279 the want of friends and kin (நட்டோர் இன்மையும் கேளிர் துன்பமும்) drives the man out. But the note inverts the proverb: ஒருபதி வாழ்தல் ஆற்றுப ... முற்றம் கடவாதோர் says that only stay-at-homes CAN bear to watch it, not that they cannot. The error is in the note, not the teaches sentence.

797 tells you to drop the friendship of பேதையார, fools by nature, and 805 tells you to read a friend's painful act as பேதைமை or பெருங்கிழமை. These are different cases, so 805 limits 797 and does not contradict it. The note also drops the பெருங்கிழமை alternative, and the teaches sentence's 'only difference is how old the bond is' misses that one verse is about character and the other about a single act.

Both set a sleeping world against one woman awake: நனந்தலை உலகமும் துஞ்சும் ஓர்யான் மன்ற துஞ்சாதேனே against மன்னுயிர் எல்லாம் துயிற்றி. The Kural qualifies the bare ஓர்யான் by giving her the night as companion (என்னல்லது இல்லை துணை), a pitied or mocked one through அளித்து, so the teaches sentence names a real change.

The match is exact: the herdsman's evening flute kills, கோவலர் கொன்றைஅம் தீம் குழல் ... உயிர் செலத் துனைதரும் மாலை against ஆயன் குழல் ... கொல்லும் படை and மாலைக்குத் தூதாகி. Natrinai 364 supplies what the couplet compresses: the herd brought home, the bells and சொல்லிய பருவம் கழிந்தன்று, which explain why a sweet sound kills.

Both are the other woman's reply to the wife's புலவி: நின் மனையோள் யாரையும் புலக்கும் எம்மை மற்று எவனோ against மனையோள் எம்மொடு புலக்கும் என்ப ... யாம் தன் பகையேம் அல்லேம் ... கொழுநனும் சாலும் தன் உடன்உறை பகையே. The two steps named in the teaches sentence (I am not singled out; the enemy is in her house) are in the Tamil.

The night path is shared (நடுஇருள் இன்னா அதர் ... அருவி நீந்தி; பானாள் ... நோக்கு அருஞ் சிறு நெறி), and the fear does pass from the girl's mouth to the friend's (என்னாவாள் என்னும் என் நெஞ்சு). But this is the stock kurinji danger of the night visit, and the claim that the friend's fear is 'usable as an argument for marriage' comes from the marker's reading, not from the quatrain.

Kuru 97 places மறை அலர் ஆகி மன்றத்து அஃதே among four scattered things but says nothing about gossip feeding or starving love, so it does not contradict கவ்வையால் கவ்விது காமம். The two voices differ, but the brief does not count different speakers' situations as a tension, and 'depends on which lover bears it' generalizes a gender rule from two poems.

The image is distinctive and shares its words: bat, mango and நெல்லி அம் புளி in both. Kuru 201's sharp-clawed, blue-winged creature eats மா then நெல்லி யம்புளி மாந்தி and hangs from bamboo, while Natrinai 87's வாவல் hangs on a மா and only dreams the sour taste (புளிச் சுவைக் கனவியாங்கு). The turn on eating against dreaming is in the verbs and matches good news against an empty day.

The formula மூத்தேம் இனி is shared exactly, and the two uses differ: a sarcastic dismissal sending the bard to the வருமுலையார் சேரி in AE 47, and a reckoning with past promises (பயமொழி ... நீத்தல் அறிந்திலேம்) in Kainnilai 45. That is a shared formula used two ways, not one verse limiting the other.

Both rank a child above another sweetness (கடுஞ்சூல் சிறுவன் முறுவல் காண்டலின் இனிதோ; அமிழ்தினும் ஆற்ற இனிது). But this is the shared topic of children's sweetness, and the teaches sentence is muddled: it calls the Kural's measure 'already a tool' in an anthology older than the couplet, as if the Kural came first.

The shoulders are shared (அளியமெல் தோளே; மென்தோள் பசப்பு), and so is the cure by his presence. But Ainkurunuru 120 does not mention pallor or seeing, and 'the wish already fulfilled in an older poem' only restates the stock situation of the third book's wasting and recovery.

The two share specific furniture: a man with a garland and bow by the செயலை, and the harvested field (வறும் புனம் காவல் விடாமை; கொய்துஒழி புனமும் நோக்கி). In both the friend sends a message closing the field tryst: the mother's guard in 376 (thurai: செறிப்பு அறிவுறீஇயது), and 'our village is the one on the hill' in Akam 38. The harvest-as-clock point is well founded.

Both use dice: Kali 136 maps each meeting to a winning throw (பத்து உருவம் பெற்றவன், மறு வித்தம்) and each parting to a lost stake, and Kural 932 has ஒன்றெய்தி நூறிழக்கும். But Kali 136 never argues net ruin, and its turn to marriage (ஏறுக தேரே) comes from fear of கௌவை, not from the Kural's arithmetic, so the teaches sentence imports a claim.

The nerunji is shared, but the uses do not meet. Kuru 202 uses the order of the plant's gifts (கட்கின் புதுமலர் முட்பயந்தாங்கு), while Kural 1120 uses only the hardness of நெருஞ்சிப் பழம் to measure her feet. 'Both poets know the nerunji as a plant that pleases first and pricks after' is not true of the couplet, which has no flower.

The paradox has the same structure: உள்ளின் உண்ணோய் மல்கும் புல்லின் மாய்வது against நீங்கின் தெறூஉம் குறுகுங்கால் தண்ணென்னும். The Kuruntokai changes the trigger from distance to thought (உள்ளின்) and the sufferer from her to herself, a real limit on the Kural's attribution of the fire to the woman.

Puram 91 makes the hiding of the virtue the gift (குறியாது ஆதல் நின்னகத்து அடக்கி ... சாதல் நீங்க). The idyll's catalogue names the virtue openly in its epithet (அமிழ்துவிளை தீங்கனி ஔவைக்கு ஈந்த அதிகன்). This is a named puram fact carried into a later list, and the shift from secret to public meaning is in the Tamil.

The phrase பிரிந்து உறை and the same flowers (அதிரல், பாதிரி) in the woman's hair are shared. In 337 the friend calls living apart a மரபு fixed when the world was made (உலகம் படைத்த காலை), while in 52 the man says நீங்கல் செல்லேம் and rebukes the heart that wants பிரிந்து உறை வாழ்க்கை. So the pair really does limit the 'custom' to a choice.

The link is real but loose. Kural 386 praises being காட்சிக்கு எளியன் and not கடுஞ்சொல்லன், while Pati 86 corrects the poet's fear of a killer (வெப்புடை ஆடூஉச் செத்தனென் மன்) by finding him தீந்தண் சாயலன். The poem is about gentleness of temper more than access, and 'fame for killing keeps suppliants away' generalizes from one poet's mistaken fear.

Both poems have the son with the father's women. But the Akananuru wife's kindness is ironic, a weapon against his denial (நின் மகன்தாய் ஆதல் புரைவது), so 'grace against fury' misreads it, and different wives in different scenes are not incompatible claims. The 'test of karpu' framing is not in either text.

The inversion is real: the couplet's sickness blooms at evening (மாலை மலரும்), while in Kali 130 the heart closes with the backwater flowers (இரும் கழி மா மலர் கூம்ப ... நெஞ்சம் அழிவொடு கூம்பும்). But the closing claim that the Kural's paradox 'depends on reversing the shore's evening closure' is unsupported, since the couplet names no shore flower, and the relation is a shared image, not a qualification.

Kali 148 gives evening its double nature: இன்புற்றார்க்கு இறைச்சியாய், பிரிந்தவர்க்கு நோய் ஆகிப் புணர்ந்தவர்க்குப் புணை ஆகி. Kural 1226 has மாலைநோய் unknown while மணந்தார் அகலாத காலை. The Kali explains why the couplet's discovery came only after he left, which neither verse says alone.

The Kural lays the cruelty on the man (கொடியார் கொடுமை, read by both shoulders and bangles), while Ainku 117 calls the state itself cruel (இன்னதாகுதல் கொடிதே) for those who do not forget him (மறவாதோர்க்கே) and names no culprit. The lost beauty is the same in both, so the contrast in where the blame is placed is specific and true.

Both read the lover from involuntary signs of the body: கண்ணும் ஆடும், வளையும் செறூஉம் against தும்மல் சினைப்பது போன்று கெடும். The contrast between hope and doubt holds, but the pairing mostly shows a shared folk sign-system, and neither verse limits the other.

Both kings lie awake in camp over the wounded: கண்படை பெறாஅது ... உள்ளியும் ... சிந்தித்தும் in Mullaippattu, and விழுப்புண் காணிய புறம்போந்து ... பள்ளி கொள்ளான் in Nedunalvadai. The contrast between inward thought with a hand on the bed and an outward round is in the lines. The final point about இன்துயில் rests on line 80, outside the printed span and of uncertain sense.

Both prize a poor meal for the regard behind it: குற்றடகு, வரகின் சொன்றி from chiefs who பாடறிந்து ஒழுகும் against உப்பிலிப் புற்கை among கிளைஞர், over royal wealth or golden-dish rice from அமரார். The swap of patron for kin is a real and specific difference between the books.

Both turn on the counsel to endure: ஆற்றென்பார் ... அன்னரே யாவர் அவரவர்க்கு against காமந் தாங்குமதி என்போர் ... அறியலர் கொல்லோ அனைமதுகையர்கொல். The venba adds evidence from the season, the bees singing in the mullai before he comes (முன்னரே ... களித்து), so the teaches sentence holds. Line 3 is obscure but not needed.

Puram 369 (மறக்களவழி) is a sustained tillage allegory ending in a request (வேழ முகவை நல்குமதி), and KN 2 has one water image, blood through burst drums like தூம்பு after கார்ப்பெயல். The contrast is real, but 'one quick simile per stanza with no request' generalizes from a single stanza, and KN 2's image is irrigation, not the threshing floor the genre name points to.

poems.note: The peacock is joined to the girl's hair by போல, and its display is a look, not an act.
The colophon thurai reads தலைமகள் where the speaker returning from work must be the man.

iraicchi.act: having fed on fish, the flock returns together to its nests at evening
iraicchi.sense: even the birds go home to their mates at dusk, while the man who left her does not think of returning (உள்ளார்)

poems.note: Lines 3 and 4 (மாண்ழாய், மார்(பு)யுஅறிம்) look corrupt, so the poem's situation is hard to fix.

iraicchi.act: at the tiger's roar the untaught male monkey hurries up the high slope together (உடன்) with his mate
iraicchi.sense: even the untaught monkey keeps his mate with him in danger, but the man went away and left her, taking her beauty and sleep

poems.note: The pairs: the crab (thief) cutting the sown sprouts is the man, the sprouts are her freshness, and the watchmen hurrying in the rain are the family's guard.

iraicchi.act: afraid of the heron's watch, the crab darts off to its hole in the kandal roots
iraicchi.sense: the man, shrinking from watching eyes, keeps away and does not come

poems.note: The heron could be read as the watching kin, which pulls toward ullurai, but only the crab's flight is firmly anchored.

iraicchi.act: the male embraces its young mate in the flowering bush
iraicchi.sense: the season's creatures are paired as he is now united with his bright-bangled girl, so his return is in time

poems.note: The hero addresses the animal (மாவே) and states his own union beside it, so the sense is nearly open.

iraicchi.act: the bee hums at the single cluster on the burnt marā and goes away unsated
iraicchi.sense: he too left before love was fulfilled, crossing that waterless waste

poems.note: The pairs: the falls is the man, the flowering vengai branch left desolate (புலம்பத் தாக்கி) is her after union, and the falls running on down the hill is his going away.
The pairs: the buffalo that breaks its tether (உழலை முருக்கிய) is the man breaking bounds, its grazing in another's field is his visits to the women, and its rest in the shade is his ease.
The pairs: the ambal is the other woman, the lotus is the wife, and the dawn blooming like a lotus is her open display. போல joins flower to flower, not to a person.
The colophon thurai reads தலைமகள் for the returning man.
